gp.text: • Gross margin increased 830 basis points to 48.3% compared to the three months ended September 2025 and includes benefits from the impact of favorable business mix and pricing, net of changes in product costs, Project Jeanius, Helly Hansen's higher margin business and lower restructuring charges compared to the three months ended September 2025.

oi.text: • Operating income increased 106% to $77.1 million, a $39.6 million increase compared to the three months ended September 2025, primarily attributable to the operating earnings growth in both the Wrangler and Helly Hansen businesses and lower restructuring charges, partially offset by the incremental costs previously allocated to the Lee ® business.

opex.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $168.5 million, from 35.6% to 38.8% of net revenues, primarily attributable to $124.4 million of increased operating expenses due to the inclusion of Helly Hansen for the entire nine-month period ende d Se ptember 2026, $33.0 million from higher investme nts in our direct-to-consumer business, demand creation and technology and $11.8 million of incremental costs previously allocated to the Lee ® business, which were partially offset by benefits from Project Jeanius.

costs.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $168.5 million, from 35.6% to 38.8% of net revenues, primarily attributable to $124.4 million of increased operating expenses due to the inclusion of Helly Hansen for the entire nine-month period ende d Se ptember 2026, $33.0 million from higher investme nts in our direct-to-consumer business, demand creation and technology and $11.8 million of incremental costs previously allocated to the Lee ® business, which were partially offset by benefits from Project Jeanius.

ga.text: During the third quarter of 2026, the Company incurred integration-related costs of $23.2 million related to Helly Hansen, comprised primarily of professional and other fees, which are reported in "selling, general and administrative expenses". We expect to incur additional costs in future periods primarily related to the information technology integration of Helly Hansen.

sga.text: During the third quarter of 2026, the Company incurred integration-related costs of $23.2 million related to Helly Hansen, comprised primarily of professional and other fees, which are reported in "selling, general and administrative expenses". We expect to incur additional costs in future periods primarily related to the information technology integration of Helly Hansen.

other_opex.text: Operating margin increased to 25.3%, compared to 24.7% for the 2025 period, due to the benefits of Project Jeanius and favorable business mix and pricing, net of changes in product costs, partially offset by other operating cost increases driven by higher investments in demand creation, technology and our direct-to-consumer businesses.

nonint.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $168.5 million, from 35.6% to 38.8% of net revenues, primarily attributable to $124.4 million of increased operating expenses due to the inclusion of Helly Hansen for the entire nine-month period ende d Se ptember 2026, $33.0 million from higher investme nts in our direct-to-consumer business, demand creation and technology and $11.8 million of incremental costs previously allocated to the Lee ® business, which were partially offset by benefits from Project Jeanius.

nonop.text: Other income (expense), net reflected a favorable chang e of $7.8 million, d riven predominantly by fore ign currency gains recognized during the three months ended September 2026 .

tax.text: In addition, we report an "Other" category to reconcile the Company's segment revenues to total revenues and segment profit to income from continuing operations before income taxes. Loss related to other revenues includes the operating results of the Musto ® and Chic ® brands, as well as other company-owned brands and private label apparel, and the Rock & Republic ® brand through the date of disposition of March 3, 2026. Results of the Musto ® brand have been included since the Acquisition on May 31, 2025. The businesses within the Other category, either individually or in the aggregate, do not meet the criteria to be considered reportable segments.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: During the nine months ended September 2026, cash provided by operating activities was $83.0 million a s compared to $109.8 million in the prior year period. Income from continuing operations in the period was impacted by ongoing transformation and Helly Hansen integration-related costs as well as incremental costs that were previously allocated to the Lee ® business that did not qualify for classification within discontinued operations. Changes in working capital balances to support the business impacted cash provided by operating activities, including cash outflows from inventory and accounts receivable which were primarily offset by cash inflows from accounts payable. The cash used by accounts receivable was driven by the growth of the business. Cash used by inventory was a result of improved sourcing lead times and proactive actions to navigate supply chain disruptions along with investment to support growth of the business. The cash provided by accounts payable reflects seasonality of the business.

capex.text: We currently expect capital expenditures to be approximately $25.0 million in 2026, primarily to support technology, distribution, manufacturing, owned retail store investments and facility improvements.

intro.text: Kontoor Brands, Inc. (NYSE: KTB) is a portfolio of three of the world’s most iconic lifestyle, outdoor and workwear brands: Wrangler ® , Lee ® and Helly Hansen ® . Kontoor Brands is a purpose-led organization focused on leveraging its global platform, strategic sourcing model and best-in-class supply chain to drive brand growth and deliver long-term value for its stakeholders. For more information about Kontoor Brands, please visit www.KontoorBrands.com.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The U.S. Wholesale channel is our largest distribution channel and accounted for approximately 64% of our net revenues in 2025.
The International Wholesale channel accounted for approximately 21% of our net revenues in 2025.
Sales to our ten largest customers accounted for 53% of total net revenues in 2025, and our top customer, Walmart, accounted for 30% of our total net revenues in 2025, 2024 and 2023.
Approximately 27% of our total net revenues in 2025 are derived from markets outside the U.S. Most of our international businesses operate in functional currencies other than the U.S. dollar.
Net revenues increased in all channels, driven by a 65% increase in International Wholesale revenues primarily attributable to Helly Hansen.

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased $267.3 million, from 31.4% to 34.5% of net revenues, driven by the impact of $193.7 million of operating expenses attributable to Helly Hansen, representing a 220 basis point increase.
Approximately 27% and 20% of our net revenues in 2025 and 2024, respectively, were generated in international markets.

The total assets and total net revenues of Helly Hansen excluded from management's assessment represent 19% and 15%, respectively, of consolidated total assets and total net revenues as of and for the year ended January 3, 2026.

The Company's largest and second-largest customers, both U.S.-based retailers, accounted for 30 % and 12 % of 2025 net revenues, respectively, and the top ten customers accounted for 53 % of 2025 net revenues.
Our largest customer accounted for 30 % of the Company's total net revenues in 2025, and 36 % in both 2024 and 2023.
Our second-largest customer accounted for 12 %, 13 %, and 11 % of total net revenues in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.

The Wrangler ® and Lee ® brands have long-term relationships with many leading brick-and-mortar and e-commerce retailers, including Amazon, Boot Barn, Target, and Walmart, whom we believe rely on these iconic brands, leading product quality and innovation to address evolving consumer needs in our product categories.
We rely on a broad base of suppliers, with the top three suppliers representing approximately 13% of total cost of goods sold.
Our revenues and profits depend on the level of consumer spending for apparel, which is sensitive to global economic conditions and other factors.

The success of our business depends on consumer spending on apparel, and there are a number of factors that influence consumer spending, including actual and perceived economic conditions, disposable consumer income, consumer discretionary spending patterns, tariffs and import/export regulations, interest rates, inflation, recessionary concerns, consumer credit availability and consumer debt levels, fuel and other energy costs, unemployment, stock market performance, weather conditions and tax rates in the international, national, regional and local markets where our products are sold.

A decision by any of our major wholesale customers to significantly decrease the volume of products purchased from us, cease purchases from us, cancel orders, reduce advertising for our products or change the manner of doing business with us, whether motivated by economic conditions, financial difficulties, competitive conditions, or otherwise, could substantially reduce net revenues and have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
The apparel industry is highly competitive, and our success depends on our ability to gauge consumer preferences and product trends, and to respond to constantly changing markets.

Although we generally have significant control over our licensees' products and advertising, we rely on our licensees for, among other things, operational and financial controls over their businesses.
In addition, we rely on our licensees to help preserve the value of our brands.
We depend on the services and management experience of our executive officers and business leaders who have substantial experience and expertise in our business.
Our future success also depends on our ability to recruit, retain and engage our personnel sufficiently.

During 2025, approximately 77% of our units were purchased from independent manufacturers primarily located in Asia, with our largest number of units sourced from Bangladesh, and substantially all of the remainder produced by Company-owned and -operated manufacturing facilities located in Mexico.

Although no single supplier is critical to our overall production needs, if we were to lose a supplier it could result in interruption of finished goods shipments to us, cancellation of orders by customers and termination of relationships.
We rely on owned or independently-operated distribution facilities to warehouse and ship product to our customers.
We rely on a limited number of North American mills for raw material sourcing, and we may not be able to obtain raw materials on a timely basis or in sufficient quantity or quality.
We rely on a limited number of North American third-party suppliers for raw materials.
The prices we pay depend on demand and market prices for the raw materials used to produce them.
Prices of purchased finished products also depend on wage rates in Asia and other geographic areas where our independent contractors are located, as well as freight costs from those regions.

While the Company has historically paid dividends to holders of our Common Stock on a quarterly basis, the declaration and payment of future dividends will depend on many factors, including, but not limited to, our earnings, financial condition, business development needs and regulatory considerations, and are at the discretion of the Board of Directors.

The Company is self-insured for a significant portion of its employee medical, workers' compensation, property and general liability exposures, and purchases from highly-rated commercial carriers to cover other risks, including property, casualty and umbrella, and to establish stop-loss limits on self-insurance arrangements.

The Company measures right-of-use operating lease assets and related operating lease liabilities based on the present value of remaining lease payments, including in-substance fixed payments, the current payment amount when payments depend on an index or rate (e.g., inflation adjustments, market renewals) and the amount the Company believes is probable to be paid to the lessor under residual value guarantees, when applicable.

The accounting for changes in the fair value of a derivative instrument (i.e., gains and losses) depends on the intended use of the derivative, whether the Company has elected to designate the derivative in a hedging relationship and apply hedge accounting and whether the hedging relationship has satisfied the criteria necessary to apply hedge accounting.
The amounts ultimately reclassified to earnings will depend on rates in effect when outstanding derivative contracts are settled.
